newsitem.title: GREECE: Papaellinas says H1 earnings up 45pct.
newsitem.headline: Papaellinas says H1 earnings up 45pct.

text.p: Cosmetics firm Papaellinas said its first half consolidated pre-tax earnings rose 45 percent to 381 million drachmas from 263 million in the first half a year earlier on sales growth of 10 percent to 6.41 billion.
"The rise in profits is the outcome of cost containment, an effort which began in June 1996," the company said.
Distribution and administrative costs as a percentage of sales dropped to 46 percent from 50.3 percent in 1996, it said, despite an increase in advertising expenses.
"If the growth rates realised in the first half persist, this year's results forecast will be revised upwards," it said.
In May, the company had forecast sales growth of 8.0 percent to 15.3 billion this year. Sales were up 20 percent in the first quarter.
